feedback: The confession follows the most consequential available contradiction: Monet could not have seen the unwrapped glass before the manager set it out, so her early-visit claim concealed later access. Taking poison and administering it are confessed acts rather than an unexpected new mechanism; the bottle, cyanide tests, access and motive were already present. Chip and Elle's speeches satisfactorily explain their documentary lies without magically clearing them by new alibis. Monet's distinction between having paid wages and having killed a person gives the ending emotional force, and it avoids treating concern for staff as absolution. The final admission is concise enough to land after the financial complexity. I found it earned and consistent with the locked accusation.
